messages.content: 你能否透過搜尋資料庫找到所有2010年由李奧納多·狄卡皮歐主演的戲劇和2012年由李奧納多·狄卡皮歐主演的喜劇電影？

function.name: imdb_find_movies_by_actor
function.description: Searches the database to find all movies by a specific actor within a certain year. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

year.description: The specific year to search in.

category.description: The category of the film (e.g. Drama, Comedy, etc). This parameter is optional.

message.reasoning:
The user asks: "Can you search the database to find all 2010 drama movies starring Leonardo DiCaprio and all 2012 comedy movies starring Leonardo DiCaprio?" They want two queries: one for 2010 drama movies with Leonardo DiCaprio, and one for 2012 comedy movies with Leonardo DiCaprio.

We have a function imdb_find_movies_by_actor that takes actor_name, year, and optional category. We need to call it twice: once with year=2010, category="Drama", and once with year=2012, category="Comedy". The actor_name is "Leonardo DiCaprio".

We should use the function calls. According to guidelines, we should not provide additional text besides the function call. So we will produce two separate function calls? The guidelines say: "When calling a function, do not add any additional text or explanation." But we can call the function multiple times. We might need to call it twice. But we cannot combine them into one call because the function only accepts one year and category. So we need to call it twice. We can output two function calls sequentially. That is allowed. Each function call is separate. So we will produce:

First call: imdb_find_movies_by_actor({"actor_name":"Leonardo DiCaprio","year":2010,"category":"Drama"})

Second call: imdb_find_movies_by_actor({"actor_name":"Leonardo DiCaprio","year":2012,"category":"Comedy"})

We should not add any other text. Just the function calls.
